title: Tennessee's 9th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The race for Tennessee's 9th Congressional District is an open-seat contest following the retirement of longtime Democratic incumbent Steve Cohen after the district was dramatically redrawn by Republican state lawmakers in May 2026. The new map splits Memphis among three congressional districts and stretches the 9th from Shelby County to the suburbs of Nashville, significantly altering its partisan composition. Competitive Republican and Democratic primaries are underway, with state Sen. Brent Taylor and state Rep. Todd Warner leading the GOP field, while state Rep. Justin Pearson and state Sen. London Lamar anchor the Democratic primary. The general election will determine whether Republicans flip a seat held by Democrats for decades in what is now considered a lean-Republican district.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were available for this race as of June 2026, as the primary election has not yet occurred and the district boundaries were just redrawn in May 2026.

candidates.name: Charlotte Bergmann
candidates.summary: Charlotte Bergmann is a lifelong Memphian, Christian conservative, and Republican candidate for Tennessee's 9th Congressional District. A former FedEx IT project manager and small business owner, she has been a perennial Republican nominee against Steve Cohen and is running again in the newly redrawn district. She focuses on crime reduction, school choice, economic growth, and America First policies.

candidates.name: Brent Taylor
candidates.summary: Brent Taylor is a Tennessee state senator representing District 31 since 2023 and a Republican candidate for the 9th Congressional District. A funeral director by trade and a former congressional candidate in 2002, he has been endorsed by U.S. Senators Marsha Blackburn and Bill Hagerty. Taylor is known for his tough-on-crime legislative record and focus on public safety, juvenile crime prevention, and conservative fiscal policy.

Described as a veteran and small business owner, he is running on a conservative platform emphasizing service, discipline, and America First principles. Thompson is one of four Republicans competing in the August 6, 2026 primary for the newly redrawn district.

candidates.name: Todd Warner
candidates.summary: Todd Warner is an 8th-generation Tennessee farmer, small business owner, and state representative for District 92 who is running for the 9th Congressional District as an America First conservative. First elected to the Tennessee House in 2020, he gained statewide attention for entering the Capitol draped in a Trump 2024 flag during the redistricting debate. Warner bills himself as a fighter against the establishment and has been endorsed by grassroots conservative groups.

candidates.name: London Lamar
candidates.summary: London Lamar is a Tennessee state senator representing District 33 since 2022 and a Democratic candidate for the 9th Congressional District. She is the youngest female and African American legislator in Tennessee State Senate history, and serves as Chair of the Senate Democratic Caucus and Chair of the Shelby County Delegation. Lamar focuses on maternal health, human trafficking prevention, criminal justice reform, voting rights, and educational equity.

candidates.summary: Justin J. Pearson is a Tennessee state representative for District 86 and a Democratic candidate for the 9th Congressional District. A Bowdoin College graduate and community organizer, he gained national attention in 2023 when he was expelled by the Republican-led House for participating in a gun control protest on the floor, then swiftly reinstated. Pearson's platform emphasizes environmental justice, ending gun violence, public education funding, economic equity, and criminal justice reform.

forecast.rationale: No public opinion polls exist for this race, the district was only redrawn in May 2026, and neither party has selected a nominee yet (primaries are August 6, 2026), all of which compel very low confidence. The race description explicitly states the newly configured TN-9 — stretching from Shelby County to Nashville suburbs after Memphis was split among three districts — is 'now considered a lean-Republican district.' Incumbent Steve Cohen is retiring, eliminating the Democrats' long-held incumbency advantage. Both parties have credible, officeholding candidates in competitive primaries (Brent Taylor/Todd Warner for Republicans; Justin Pearson/London Lamar for Democrats), which suggests both sides will field a viable general election candidate. No polling data exists to quantify the shift. The qualitative structural signal from the redistricting points to a meaningful Republican advantage, but the total absence of polling, the unsettled primaries, and the historic Democratic lean of the area under previous maps all warrant treating this as a lean Republican seat with substantial uncertainty.
